intended_object: The second projection M × N → N, viewed as a monotone monoid homomorphism (a morphism of ordered monoids), where M × N has the componentwise product order. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition reuses `MonoidHom.snd`, so the underlying map is (a, b) ↦ b, which preserves 1 and multiplication. Monotonicity comes from `MonoidHom.snd_mono`, which holds for the product order (`Prod.le_def`). So the definition gives exactly the canonical projection as an `OrderMonoidHom`, at the level of monoids with no commutativity required.

There is one small point. The shared `variable` line asks for `PartialOrder α`, while `snd` itself only needs `Preorder α`. The stronger assumption is there because the lexicographic maps later in the same section (e.g. `inlₗ` via `Prod.Lex.toLexOrderHom`) need it. Ordered monoids in the literature are normally partially ordered anyway, so this is not a real loss of generality. Mathlib has no other definition of this projection as an ordered monoid homomorphism.
